title: Study Design and Rationale of a Dose‐Ranging Trial of <scp>LX4211</scp>, a Dual Inhibitor of <scp>SGLT1</scp> and <scp>SGLT2</scp>, in Type 2 Diabetes Inadequately Controlled on Metformin Monotherapy

sections.abstract: <jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:label /><jats:p>Sodium‐glucose cotransporters 1 (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT1</jats:styled-content>) and 2 (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT2</jats:styled-content>) are the major cellular transporters responsible for gastrointestinal (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GI</jats:styled-content>) glucose absorption and renal glucose reabsorption, respectively. <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LX4211</jats:styled-content>, a dual inhibitor of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT1</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT2</jats:styled-content>, reduces glucose absorption from the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GI</jats:styled-content> tract and enhances urinary glucose excretion. Although several <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT2</jats:styled-content>‐selective inhibitors have been tested in large phase 2 studies, dual inhibition of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT1</jats:styled-content> and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SGLT2</jats:styled-content> is novel at this stage of drug development, and it has implications for clinical‐trial design. In this article, we describe the design and rationale of a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled, parallel group study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LX4211</jats:styled-content> in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus who have inadequate glycemic control on metformin monotherapy. The primary endpoint is the change in glycated hemoglobin A<jats:sub>1c</jats:sub> from baseline to week 12. Secondary endpoints include the proportion of subjects achieving a glycated hemoglobin A<jats:sub>1c</jats:sub> value of <7%, change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose and postprandial glucose (as part of an oral glucose tolerance test), body weight, and blood pressure. Safety is evaluated with particular focus on hypoglycemia, <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GI</jats:styled-content> symptoms, and incidence of genitourinary tract infections.</jats:p></jats:sec>
